brief.data: A replay covering Sep 11–17, 2026, at 10-minute steps (1,008 frames), from 46 volunteer-hosted sensors plus 1 regulatory monitor. prompt:
I need the front end for Hazereel. A playback tool for a volunteer-run neighborhood air-quality network that replays past days of readings from members' backyard sensors as narrated, time-stepped sequences anyone can watch at their own pace.

Who's using it: Teodoro Vance, a retired schoolteacher and volunteer board member of the Eastbank Clean Air Collective. He's comfortable with spreadsheets but isn't a data person. He knows the neighborhoods and most of the sensor hosts personally.

What they're doing right now: Teodoro is speaking at Thursday's city council meeting about clean-air shelters. He's watching the collective's replay of the September wildfire-smoke week, which another volunteer narrated in chapters. He keeps slowing down through the night of September 14, when readings near the elementary school spiked hours before the official regional monitor reacted. He scrubs back and forth to find the exact hour, rewatches the narrator's chapter on the school, notes timestamps, and decides which 90 seconds he'll ask council to watch.

What's in the system at this point: A replay covering Sep 11–17, 2026, at 10-minute steps (1,008 frames), from 46 volunteer-hosted sensors plus 1 regulatory monitor. Each reading has PM2.5 in µg/m³, a humidity-corrected value, the sensor host's block, and an offline/online flag (5 sensors dropped out mid-week). Narration recorded by volunteer Ama Lindqvist runs 14 minutes in 6 chapters (e.g. 'The smoke arrives', 'Night of the 14th at Linden Elementary', 'When the regional alert came'). Captions and a transcript are included. Key moments: peak 287 µg/m³ at 2:40 a.m. Sep 15 near Linden Elementary, and the regional alert issued at 7:10 a.m. There are two older replays, the July 4 fireworks 2026 and the 2025 Harlow Fire, and Teodoro has 3 bookmarks saved in this one.

Build it as a working web app, opened in the state that person would see at that moment. No backend: use realistic mock data (no lorem ipsum, no placeholder names), and make the interactive parts actually work client-side.

Use whatever framework and tooling you like. When you're done there must be a static production build in ./out with ./out/index.html as the entry point. It will be served from the root of a plain static file server (no rewrites, no server code) and viewed in a desktop browser at 1440×900.
